fix round 1 rule: In spawn.run_worker's review and spec_review branch, contracts.process must run AFTER parse_failed and existing_result are computed and must never replace a verdict the worker already posted: when existing_result carries a verdict, keep it and skip recovery; recovery (active mode only) runs solely when no verdict exists anywhere; add a test where a mid-run posted approve survives a verdict-less final response with contracts active.

result.summary: Fix correctly reorders contracts.process to run after parse_failed/existing_result are computed, adds preserve=True to skip recovery entirely when an existing posted verdict is found, and keeps the worker's own posted verdict instead of a later verdict-less or conflicting final response for both review and spec_review roles. New tests (test_active_contract_preserves_mid_run_verdict_without_recovery, test_active_contract_does_not_resume_when_final_verdict_exists) cover the required scenario across both roles and several final-response shapes (missing verdict, non-JSON text, conflicting verdict), and correctly assert recover() is never called, status ends done, and decision_log records a deterministic-ok output_contract row. Verified against contracts.py's recover()/process() short-circuiting on preserve and against bus.post_result's status/confidence/provenance defaults. Only a minor asymmetry noted below (non-blocking).

comments.issue: When existing_result already carries a verdict, bus.post_result is only re-invoked for role=="review"; the spec_review branch never re-posts. This works today only because bus.post_result already stamped status="done" and confidence/provenance defaults during the mid-run post, so nothing currently relies on this second call for spec_review. Worth a comment or symmetric handling so a future change to post_result's defaults (or to how existing_result gets populated) doesn't silently leave a spec_review task not marked done.
